Salam,

  • Context: the 27 August five month review put hard numbers on the intake problem. 65 percent of inbound calls are missed and 78 percent of those arrive outside office hours. Only 20 percent of inbound texts and Instagram messages get a human reply. Against $8,200 of ad spend and 84 leads in the period, that intake gap is what is driving cost per lead up, not the campaigns. Callbacks are currently made outside GHL, so there is no record of who was chased or how many times.

  •  Log every call attempt as a note on the opportunity so attempt counts are queryable. Add a Junk stage so spam and marketing calls are filtered out instead of inflating lead counts.

  • Automation: send a second missed call text five minutes after the first to widen the engagement window on the after hours volume. Build a notification workflow that alerts the team member (assigned or Luis) when a lead responds, so replies are picked up in real time rather than at the next inbox check. Push the centralised lead inbox and the GHL mobile app so those alerts actually land.

  • Done = the GHL pipeline carries Attempted Contact, Engaged and Junk stages, every call attempt writes a note on the opportunity, a second missed call text fires five minutes after the first, team members are notified on lead responses, Luis is working callbacks inside GHL, and the missed call backlog is cleared.

Salam,

  • Context. MedStation was closed on 7 September. Before 9am Renata had already answered three inbound leads by hand, because nothing replies automatically when the clinic is shut, and she said she had also picked up a message the previous night. Her words were that we should have messages after business hours too. This is the gap this item was opened for, now showing up with real patients on the other end.
  • The policy Sohib set the same morning. Do not try to hold the conversation out of hours. Tell the lead we are closed, say we will be in contact during business hours, and invite them to leave what they are looking for so the team has something to work from when it opens.
  • What was actually built on the day. Ahmed built a closed today message in GoHighLevel on 7 September. It fires on WhatsApp only. To avoid double messaging he put the other messaging workflows into draft for the day so that only the holiday workflow responded, and said they would be switched back on the next day. Confirm those workflows are live again, a manual switch back is exactly the kind of step that gets missed.
  • Deliverable one, full channel coverage. Sohib asked for the trigger to cover missed calls and Instagram DMs as well as WhatsApp, and Ahmed agreed. A lead who rings a closed clinic today gets nothing at all.
  • Deliverable two, make it a condition and not a one off build. The brief already on this item is that business hours belong as a condition inside each messaging workflow, not as a parallel after hours workflow. The 7 September holiday message was hand built for a single day, which is the opposite pattern. Drive the closed day case from a dated holiday list the team can edit, so the next closure needs no developer.
  • Deliverable three, one message per lead. Somebody who rings, gets no answer and then sends a WhatsApp message out of hours must receive one closed notice, not one per channel. Deduplicate across the channels before this goes live.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No client dependency and nothing to wait on, this can start immediately. The hours are 8am to 5pm Eastern, Monday to Friday, the same window already settled for the escalation workflows on this board, so build the condition once and reference it from both rather than defining it twice. Do not leave any workflow sitting in draft after a closure.
  • done = a message sent outside business hours, a missed call outside business hours and an Instagram DM outside business hours each produce exactly one automatic closed notice to the lead, a closure date can be added by the team without a rebuild, every messaging workflow is confirmed live again, and the test results are posted here.

body:
Salam,

  • Context. The 3 September MedStation go live call moved lead escalation off user assignment triggers and onto message status triggers, and Sohib wrote the build out as point three of his recap in the GHL Dev chat the same day. Today a lead who calls and gets no answer, or texts and gets no reply, falls through with nobody told about it. The 4 September call then specified the trigger conditions, which are carried below.
  • Workflow one, missed call textback. Build it to the same pattern already running for Maadi Law: an inbound call that is not answered triggers an automatic message back to the caller. Reuse the Maadi Law build as the reference rather than starting from a blank workflow.
  • Workflow two, missed message textback. Trigger on a lead sending us a message that nobody replies to inside the escalation window, and send an automatic acknowledgement. This is the half that does not exist anywhere yet, so it needs specifying as well as building.
  • The escalation window, settled on 4 September. The internal alert must fire only when no staff reply has been sent within one hour of the patient’s message. As currently built the notification triggers on the contact replying at all, which means the team is alerted even when somebody has already answered. Correct that condition, it is the specific defect named on the call.
  • Business hours, one condition not two workflows. The one hour timer applies during business hours only, 8am to 5pm Eastern, Monday to Friday. Outside those hours the alert waits until the next business morning rather than disturbing anyone.   • Report back with a number, not an impression. Post WhatsApp conversations started, phone calls, and cost per conversation for the first full week after the change, split by Google and Meta, so the pivot to WhatsApp is judged on outcome rather than on the fact that it was made.
  • done = broad match and the single phone call conversion goal are either applied or declined in writing here, and one full week of WhatsApp conversations, calls and cost per conversation after the 8 September change is posted for both Google and Meta.

creator: Nacer Amrouch
body:
Salam,

  • Context. On 8 September Sohib said in the Web and SEO group that the lack of attention from him and Nacer has been hurting clients, and gave two live examples: Quality HVAC (Fibid) on zero calls in August and still zero in September, and Liferun with a Google Business Profile basically empty of photos. His point was not those two accounts. It was that he cannot hold every operation in his head, that he had a hard call when HVAC called Flow out for missing an entire month of a dead profile, and that there are likely more gaps nobody has found. He asked outright what needs to happen here. This item is the answer, so the next gap gets caught by a process rather than by a client complaint.
  • Deliverable one, write the review checklist. One short written checklist run per client, covering at minimum: Google Business Profile verification state and suspension check, categories, service area, hours, phone number, photo count and last post date, monthly call and message volume against the previous month, site uptime and core page health, form submissions actually arriving, and whether the last client report went out. Every gap named on 8 September would have been caught by the call volume line and the last post line alone.
  • Deliverable two, put the review on a fixed rhythm. Run the checklist per client on a weekly cycle with a named owner and record the result somewhere Naz and Sohib can read without asking. Hashir also offered to send a weekly update directly into each client chat, which is the client facing half of the same rhythm. Both halves are required, because an internal check nobody reports on is how a dead month goes unnoticed and a client update with no check behind it is just reassurance.
  • Deliverable three, roll out Google Business Profile posting. Once the assets exist, start the posting cadence across the client base. The Posting subitems already exist per client on the GBP items, so populate those rather than opening new ones.
  • done = the frame.io seat and the per client photo and video folder both exist, a written checklist is agreed, one full pass has been run across every Web and SEO client with the results recorded, the weekly rhythm and its owner are set, and Google Business Profile posting is live for every client with assets.
